mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% over two consecutive quarters signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of FEDFUNDS > 2.0% tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 1% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in the same month signals a significant labor market deterioration, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month AND PAYEMS monthly change < -100000
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% during a recessionary regime (UNRATE > 5%) signals an aggressive monetary easing, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the trend by more than 5% for three consecutive months signals heightened precautionary saving, which reduces consumer spending and thus corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > trend by >5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% and 8% respectively signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, increasing recession probability and depressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% AND HOUST monthly change < -8%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered months.
